title: MECHANISM FEMALE OVARIAN/MENSTRUAL CYCLE -- estradiol positive-feedback LH-surge bistable switch
task: Build the female HPG cyclic oscillator delta EXPLICITLY scoped OUT of docs/MECHANISM_REPRODUCTIVE_HPG.md (the male axis), which named the periovulatory LH surge 'a genuinely different (bistable-switch, threshold-not-sharply-defined) mathematical object than a negative-feedback steady state' and left it OPEN. FALSIFIER (symmetric): reproduce the phase structure (follicular -> LH surge -> luteal -> menstruation) AND the estradiol positive-feedback sign-flip that produces the surge, while a purely-negative-feedback model -- forced to its strongest fair form (steepness x operating-point x delay, 90 configs) -- must FAIL, via the geometric fact that a monotonically decreasing function of E2 composed with E2's own unimodal trajectory has its minimum (not maximum) exactly where E2 peaks. Also test the GnRH-pulse-frequency -> LH/FSH-ratio coding (reusing the male doc's own validated transfer function with zero new parameters) across PCOS/normal/hypothalamic-amenorrhea, and the menopause-transition FSH rise as an explicitly DECORRELATED (loss-of-restraint, not bistable-switch) mechanism.
confidence_tier: In-vivo-anchored, population/literature-level -- same tier as MECHANISM_REPRODUCTIVE_HPG.md and every sibling endocrine doc in this repo. Real human serial/frequent-sampling data across 15 of 17 citations (n ranging 4-293); no subject-specific hormone panel exists for subject2. Two citations (Knobil 1980, Wildt 1981 E2) are REUSED from MECHANISM_REPRODUCTIVE_HPG.md and independently spot-re-verified live this session, not blindly trusted.
script_provenance: Self-contained numpy/scipy (scipy.integrate.solve_ivp, RK45), no external data inputs, no OpenSim call. Deterministic: 2 independent runs produce byte-identical JSON (verified via diff this session). Zero NaN/Inf across the full output JSON tree (checked programmatically, all leaf floats). Runs in a few seconds.
raw_fetch_logs: All 17 citations fetched live this session via NCBI E-utilities (esearch to find/disambiguate candidate PMIDs, esummary to disambiguate multi-candidate author searches, efetch rettype=abstract retmode=text for full verbatim abstract text) using curl directly against eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov -- not WebFetch-summarized, not recalled from memory. 15/17 citations returned full verbatim abstract text with the specific numeric findings quoted in the doc. 1/17 (Young & Jaffe 1976, PMID 767352) returned only a methods-only abstract (no numeric result in the PubMed-indexed text) -- disclosed as a genuine gap, not papered over: the abstract confirms the paper/authors/dose-range exist and are correctly cited, but the actual strength-duration numeric finding is in the paper's results/tables, not its indexed abstract. 2/17 (Knobil 1980 PMID 6766566, Wildt 1981 PMID 6783398) are REUSED from the sibling MECHANISM_REPRODUCTIVE_HPG.md doc and were independently spot-re-verified live this session (not blindly trusted) -- both matched that doc's own citation exactly.

gates_summary.self_correction_disclosed: An earlier version of the adversary trough-alignment check compared every config's LH trough against the un-shifted E2-peak day, wrongly flagging 54/90 delay>0 configs as 'misaligned'. Diagnosed via the model's own geometric argument (a time-delay shifts the trough by exactly +delay; it does not anchor it back to the un-delayed E2 peak), confirmed the shift matched +delay_h exactly for all 54 flagged rows, then corrected the check to compare against the right reference point (t_E2peak+delay). The load-bearing falsification claim (the adversary's PEAK never aligns with E2's peak, 0/90 configs) was never affected by this bug -- only a secondary, more precise diagnostic metric was. Caught by running the check against its own stated prediction, not smoothed over.

function<->dysfunction: PCOS (persistently fast tonic GnRH pulse frequency -> elevated LH:FSH ratio, Waldstreicher 1988 + Rebar 1976), hypothalamic amenorrhea (persistently slow/suppressed pulse frequency -> lowest LH:FSH ratio of all 7 tested conditions + E2 never reaches the surge threshold, Reame 1985 + Khoury 1987), menopause transition (explicitly DECORRELATED loss-of-restraint mechanism, not the bistable switch, Burger 1998 + Burger 1999) -- all three built as parameter variations of the SAME reused machinery (the frequency-coding transfer function and/or the D(t)-gated secretion law), not three separately hacked rules.

recall_drift_detail: TWO self-generated (not literature-recall) errors were caught this session by machine-checking rather than trusting prose, and are disclosed rather than silently fixed: (1) This session's own draft geometric-argument text initially asserted 't_lh_trough_day == t_e2_peak_day for every one of the 90 swept configs' without accounting for the applied time-delay's effect on where the trough lands. Caught by machine-running the check against its own claim; see gates_summary.self_correction_disclosed for the full diagnosis and fix. (2) A FABRICATED DOI: a first draft of the WHO 1980 citation (PMID 6775535) guessed a plausible-looking DOI (10.1016/0002-9378(80)90133-9) that was never actually present in either the live-fetched abstract text (which, unlike all 16 other fetches, printed no DOI: line) or a follow-up esummary check of the record's authoritative articleids field (only pubmed+pii listed, no doi type -- and the real PII's last digit, -7, does not even match the guessed DOI's -9). Caught by re-querying esummary rather than trusting a pattern-matched guess; corrected to doi=null + the real PII. Separately, no external-literature NUMERIC-VALUE drift was detected in the 16 citations with full verbatim abstract text (every quoted number was read directly from the live-fetched abstract, not from memory) -- the 1 citation without abstract text (Young & Jaffe 1976) was correspondingly NOT used for any numeric claim beyond the disclosed dose-range figures actually present in its abstract.
honest_gaps: E2(t)/P4(t) are prescribed (landmark-calibrated) forcing functions, not derived from a follicle-growth/steroidogenesis ODE -- a disclosed reduction, tested for robustness (9 shape variants) but not eliminated as a modeling choice.

The abruptness gate is directionally but not numerically matched to Hoff/Quigley/Yen 1983's real ~28-30x ratio (model achieves 8.64x) -- a separate fast pituitary self-priming mechanism, not built here, would be needed to close this gap.

Young & Jaffe 1976's own indexed abstract lacks the numeric strength-duration result; the ~200pg/mL/48h threshold used is field-consensus attribution cross-checked against Chang & Jaffe 1978's independent 271pg/mL anchor, not independently re-derived from Young & Jaffe's own text this session.

PCOS is modeled only via the frequency-coding transfer function; Rebar 1976's own finding that the positive-feedback switch remains intact in PCOS is disclosed but not modeled as a separate mechanism.

The menopause-transition FSH formula is checked for ordering/jump-location against one paper's (Burger 1998) 4-stage means, not fit; Burger 1999 (the correlation cross-check) shares senior authorship/lab, not a fully independent second cohort.

The amplitude gate (unlike the phase gate, which is 100% robust across 27 secretion-law configs) has a real gain-dependent failure boundary; DEFAULT_PARAMS sits with a disclosed ~2x margin above it, not at a knife-edge, but amplitude is not claimed to be parameter-independent.
No graph-edge write this session (isolation rule); circadian coupling not attempted; small samples throughout multiple source papers (n=4-24) are point estimates, not distributions.
